item.title: Dueling rallies thrust deep-red Lone Star town into the center of the political universe
item.description: Dueling rallies in Lubbock put the Texas Senate race between Ken Paxton and James Talarico on full display as Trump joined the Republican side.
item.content:encoded:
LUBBOCK, Texas — Two rallies, two crowds and two very different visions for Texas converged in deep-red Lubbock on Tuesday night as Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico made their cases to voters.

Trump supporters camped out at Lubbock’s Civic Center as early as Monday night, calling the event a "once-in-a-lifetime experience." About four miles away, roughly 4,000 Talarico supporters descended on the neighborhood around the Fiesta Center.

The rallies put Lubbock’s political identity on display. Long a ruby-red Republican stronghold, the city is now a battleground in a Senate race in which polls show Talarico narrowly leading Paxton.

Outside Paxton’s rally, supporters remained confident the Lone Star State would stay red.

Jenny, who traveled from Brownsville, dismissed the idea that the race was close.

"What else do the Democrats have? They have Talarico going against Paxton," she told Fox News Digital. "All they’ve got is the ability to try and make people think that it’s close and there is no point in voting."

"No, it’s not close," Jenny added. "Paxton is going to wipe the floor with him."

MEET THE VOTERS WHO COULD BREAK THE GOP’S DECADESLONG GRIP ON A REPUBLICAN STRONGHOLD

Eric, a Lubbock resident, also predicted a Republican win, saying Democratic policies do not align with his views.

"Most of the Democrats that you talk to, when you start talking common sense to them, a lot of them, they don’t know if it’s a red or a blue policy, and a lot of them line up with red as well," he said. "It’s gonna stay red, absolutely."

Nathan, from Milton, said he wants to preserve what he sees as Texas’ traditional values, including gun rights and opposition to abortion.

"I want to make sure we are keeping all the normal values that we have in Texas," he said. "I want to make sure that we are keeping our guns, we are keeping our safety, keeping abortion as far away from Texas and do everything we can to keep Texas, Texas."

Across town, Talarico supporters said Trump’s appearance alongside Paxton showed Republicans were worried about losing ground in a reliably red state.

"Trump’s in Lubbock? Trump’s in Lubbock, Texas? He’s scared, he is scared," one supporter told Fox News Digital.

Natalie, from Friona, also viewed the same-day rallies as a sign of nervousness.

"I think they have to be nervous, and I think it’s performative, like to come the exact same day as he is here," she said. "I really hope so, and looking at all of this, I think it is."

DEEP IN TRUMP COUNTRY, A NEW GENERATION REVEALS THE DIVIDE BEHIND TEXAS’ TIGHT SENATE RACE

Elias, a Lubbock resident, said Paxton’s reliance on Trump reflected poorly on the Republican candidate. He pointed to Paxton’s past controversies and impeachment by the Texas House.

"I think it shows that Paxton is a weak leader," Elias said. "He had a chance to kind of redeem himself despite his ugly past, but he’s not a man, he can’t stand up for himself. He needs daddy Trump to come and support him."

Other Talarico supporters said they believed Texas could turn blue. Jessica, from Lubbock, and Shelby, from Houston, cited dissatisfaction with how the state has been run in recent years.

"I think they’re scared that it is going to flip, and I believe it will because of how they have run this county the last few years," they said.

Christine and John, both from Lubbock, also predicted change. "They are nervous, and this is the year we are going to change it all," Christine said.

Paloma, a Lubbock resident, put their optimism plainly: "This is the year that we flip blue. We are definitely going to flip the state."

item.title: WWE's Crown Jewel premium live event 'moved to a new venue' as tensions increase in the Middle East
item.description: WWE Crown Jewel is moving from its Riyadh venue after Houthi airstrikes on Saudi Arabia's King Khalid International Airport heightened safety concerns.
item.content:encoded:
WWE premium live event Crown Jewel, which was set to take place on Nov. 7 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, is moving to a new venue amid escalating tensions in the Middle East.

Riyadh Season, which is the entertainment festival held in the city across several months and is organized by Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority, made the announcement in a statement posted to social media on Wednesday.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

"We would like to inform you that ‘WWE Crown Jewel’ has been moved to a new venue," the statement posted to X read. "All ticket holders will receive a full refund, and tickets will be re-released to everyone within the next 48 hours."

OutKick Dropkick reached out to WWE for further information.

Crown Jewel was set to be one of three events being held in Saudi Arabia this season and was set to take place at Riyadh Season Stadium. WWE’s premium live event calendar kicked off with the Royal Rumble in January – the first traditional Royal Rumble to be held in the country. The country also hosted Night of Champions in June.

In between the events was President Donald Trump’s decision to hit Iran with airstrikes, sparking months of unrest in the region. The U.S., Israel, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Bahrain, Houthis in Yemen and Iran have all been involved in the conflict since late February.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Tensions were heightened earlier this month when Houthis struck King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, leaving more than a dozen dead. The attack quickly put Crown Jewel in the focus of the pro wrestling world as worries began to increase over WWE personnel possibly being put into a dangerous situation.

Those concerns only increased as the U.S. Embassy in Saudi Arabia ordered non-emergency U.S. government employees and U.S. government employee family members to leave Saudi Arabia "due to safety risks."

"Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," the embassy said. "The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area."

The U.S. State Department also updated travel advisories for several Middle Eastern countries, including Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Syria and Yemen, to Level 4 and urged Americans not to travel there over fears of Houthi attacks and threats against Americans.

Saudi Arabia said Monday its coalition shot down three missiles fired by Houthis toward the Eastern Province.

"Air defenses intercepted and destroyed 3 ballistic missiles launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the eastern region," Saudi military spokesman Col. Turki al-Malki said in a post on X.

WrestleMania 43 – WWE’s biggest event of the year – was still set to take place in Saudi Arabia next year.

item.title: Madison Beer heckled by Chargers fans during Disney show, Madden impressions & Rays reporter Aileen Hnatiuk!
item.description: The final Hump Day of October brings Madison Beer hearing "Fix the Chargers!" from fans at Disneyland as Justin Herbert's NFL season spirals.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

Final Hump Day of October, boys and girls. Feels like we just started what is, objectively, the greatest month of the year — and now it's just about over.

Sad. You know what's even worse? An even bigger punch to the gut?

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Look at what I walked into at the Lowe's down the street yesterday afternoon:

Disgusting behavior. I get it, by the way. Don't get me wrong. Save your, "This is how advertising works!" emails. I know. I gotcha.

Doesn't make it any more palatable, though. Lowe's has already turned the page on Halloween. In fact, not pictured is the giant tent out in the parking lot that they've already got set up.

That's the Christmas tree (!!!) tent, and it's been up since last week. As Mike Gundy once said, "Where are we at in society today?!"

Anyway ...

Welcome to a Hump Day Nightcaps — the one where Justin Herbert's fiancee, Madison Beer, hears it from sad Chargers fans during her performance at Disneyland.

Happiest Place on Earth my butt!

What else? I've also got Nic Cage portraying the late John Madden (I use 'portray' loosely), Rays fans under fire for being swallowed by Brewers fans, and OutKick legend Aileen Hnatiuk may have single-handedly willed Tampa to a Game 5 last night.

You'll see.

OK, grab you a pumpkin beer for our final Hump Day class of October, and let's get this show on the road.

DOLPHINS AVOID 0-17 CRISIS, PICK UP FIRST WIN OF SEASON AGAINST STRUGGLING JETS ON THE ROAD

No stalling today. As I've said, time ain't our side right now. We've all got things to do and pumpkins to carve before Mariah Carey invades our homes for the next two months.

So, let's start with the NFL ...

If you would've told me in August that the Colts and Chargers would be the two most embarrassing teams in the league by Halloween, I would've said you were NUTS. I'd just naturally assume it was my Dolphins, but they've been more than respectable this season.

Most ethical tank job of all time. Well done, Miami.

Yesterday, the Colts started their fire-sale, and I assume the Chargers ain't far behind. They're coming off a bye week, and now get to play the Rams. When they lose, I wouldn't be surprised to see Mike McDaniel canned.

ROB GRONKOWSKI CALLS CHARGERS 'PROBABLY THE BIGGEST MESS IN THE NFL' RIGHT NOW AFTER ROUGH START

Even as a miserable Dolphins fan who was ready to see McDaniel go, I'll admit, I'm a little shocked at just how bad they've looked on offense this season. For years, the debate was, "Tua or Herbert?" The answer, it seems, is neither. They both stink.

Trust me, I have a ton of Herbert in fantasy this year, and my teams STINK. He's looked genuinely terrible.

Which brings me to his fiancée, Madison Beer ...

Welcome to hell, Madison! And I ain't talking about Disneyland:

"FIX THE CHARGERS!" has got to be such a deflating thing to hear if you're Madison Beer performing at Disneyland. She signed on for a great season, and it's just been pure misery week in and week out.

Madison and Herbert were all the rage in the offseason. We couldn't get enough of them. They had the NFL world wrapped around their fingers, and now she's having to deal with questions that should be directed at the front office.

Sad. Chin up, Madison! Surely it can't get any worse, right ...

Can't say I blame Justin here. Lord knows it's how I'd handle an 0-5 start. I respect the choice of beverage, too. Miller Lite is elite. Nobody does the aluminum bottle game better.

Moving on ...

Speaking of doing things better, let's check in with Nicolas Cage as his new John Madden biopic gets set to hit your Prime Video streams in just three shorts weeks!

I'm gonna level with everyone ... that's just an awful John Madden impression. I'm not sure we can even call it an impression? I think it's just Nicolas Cage ... talking like Nicolas Cage?

He didn't even attempt to sound like Madden. I don't get it? And how about the dude playing Pat Summerall? He's getting a pass today because everyone is focused on how bad Cage's Madden is, but that's equally horrible.

If you had me close my eyes and gave me a thousand guesses at who that was speaking, I would never land on John Madden. Ever. I'd say it was Nicolas Cage ... because it sounds like Nicolas Cage.

For those too young to remember, this was peak John Madden:

Goodness. Did we have it all, or what? Those were the days. Our family grew up eating turducken on Thanksgiving, and it was all because of Madden. He was the best.

PS: Turducken? Good. The process of putting it together? Disgusting. But still, you do it right, and it's delicious.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Hump Day class into a one final October Hump Day night. First up? I'll be the first to admit, I was wrong about this World Series.

I figured Fox would get slammed in the ratings with the Rays and Brewers, but the numbers are out, and they're actually really solid:

Look, they aren't Yankees or Dodgers numbers — or Phillies, Red Sox or Cubs — but it's a really strong start. Over 12 million for Game 1, and nearly 11 million for Game 2? I'd that in a heartbeat, especially given Game 2 went up against college football.

Game 3 will be interesting to watch because it went up against Cowboys-Eagles. There's a reason the Cowboys are in primetime six times a year.

But still, this is a win for for MLB.

Not really a win for the owners, though. The whole "small market teams can't compete, on and off the field" argument has sort of fallen apart this postseason. I just think it's gonna be a tough sell when the lockout inevitably begins in five weeks.

Sadly, I think that means we're in for a really long offseason. We'll see.

Next? While the TV ratings look good, the optics inside the Trop on Monday ... did not:

Lordy. That's A LOT of Brew Crew on my screen. A lot. I know it was a blowout. I know it's a big park. But still, I can't imagine Rays ownership loved seeing that.

But hey! We've got a Game 5 tonight. Still time to show out, Rays fans! Let's extend this season to a Game 6, fellas. Again, it might be the last time we get baseball for a while.

OK, that's it for today. Good final October Hump Day, everyone. Solid work.

On the way out, here's Tampa reporter Aileen Hnatiuk, who went mega-viral a few years back as a Saints reporter, willing the Rays to a big Game 4 win in extras.

Welcome back, Aileen.

See you tomorrow.

item.title: 'Radical Left Lunatic' judge Trump wanted impeached takes up Ilhan Omar warrant fight
item.description: Judge James Boasberg, a frequent Trump legal foe, now oversees the fight to unseal the FBI search warrant used in the raid on Rep. Ilhan Omar's home.
item.content:encoded:
A federal judge who has become a frequent legal thorn in the side of President Donald Trump and his allies is now presiding over a fight to unseal the warrant used to search the home of Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn.

The battle over whether to unseal the search warrant comes amid two separate federal investigations into the Democratic congresswoman stemming from concerns about discrepancies between financial disclosures filed a year apart and allegations that her father committed fraud when completing immigration paperwork. Omar immigrated to the United States from Somalia in 1995, when she was 12 years old. Investigators are examining whether her father misstated her age on his citizenship paperwork in 2000, potentially allowing her to obtain citizenship through him as a minor.

Trump, a longtime foe of the progressive congresswoman, has been vocal in his attacks against Omar, having also accused her of committing immigration fraud by allegedly marrying her brother — referring to her first husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi. In the weeks following the Oct. 12 raid on Omar's Washington, D.C., home, Trump called for Omar to be "put in jail."

TRUMP SAYS ILHAN OMAR COULD GO TO JAIL OR BE DEPORTED, CALLS HER ‘A DISGRACE TO OUR COUNTRY’

But the fight over whether to unseal the records is being overseen by Chief Judge James Boasberg of the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, an Obama appointee and longtime target of Trump. In March 2025, after Boasberg temporarily blocked deportation flights carrying alleged Venezuelan gang members, Trump called him a "Radical Left Lunatic of a Judge, a troublemaker and agitator" and called for his impeachment. Trump also accused Boasberg of bias, saying it was "virtually impossible for me to get an Honest Ruling in D.C."

The raid on Omar’s home came just weeks before the midterm elections, as alleged fraud in Minnesota’s social services programs had become a major political issue in the state.

ILHAN OMAR'S TURBULENT WEEK EXPLAINED: THE DUELING PROBES THAT THREW THE SOMALI-BORN PROGRESSIVE INTO CHAOS

Days after Department of Homeland Security Investigations and the FBI conducted a raid on Omar's home under a search warrant issued by U.S. Magistrate Judge Matthew Sharbaugh, three separate requests were made to unseal the warrant — by the New York Times; Judicial Watch, a conservative watchdog group; and 14 press organizations.

Boasberg ordered the Justice Department to defend its position on keeping the warrant sealed in response to a consolidated request from the Times and 14 press organizations by Oct. 22, but he extended the deadline following a Justice Department request to wait until the search warrant was "fully executed."

The Justice Department argued that releasing the information could compromise the integrity of the investigation.

"This request sounds rash because it is rash," Pirro wrote. "The Court should reject it without prejudice for renewal after the search warrant has been fully executed and a charging decision is made public."

The filing indicated that the Justice Department was still in the process of executing the search warrant, while other details about the investigation and warrant records remained redacted from the public record.

But the Times and other media groups argue that the physical search occurred weeks ago and that any sensitive information in the warrant should be redacted rather than the entire warrant being withheld.

Meanwhile, Omar is engaged in a separate dispute with the Justice Department. Her attorneys have demanded the return of property seized from her home, arguing that agents violated protections for her congressional work. They have also alleged that agents failed to provide her with a copy of the warrant and prevented her from contacting her attorneys during the search.

FEDERAL AGENTS SEIZE PHONE OF REP ILHAN OMAR IN RAID TIED TO IMMIGRATION FRAUD PROBE

Boasberg’s oversight of efforts to unseal the records follows a series of decisions that have drawn criticism from Trump and his allies. In June 2025, he ordered federal agencies to preserve Signal messages exchanged by senior officials while discussing U.S. military strikes in Yemen, saying the communications could constitute federal records. During the Biden administration's Arctic Frost investigation, he signed nondisclosure orders barring phone carriers from notifying Republican lawmakers that prosecutors had subpoenaed their records.

Boasberg also drew criticism over his sentencing of former FBI attorney Kevin Clinesmith. Clinesmith pleaded guilty to altering an email used in an application to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court to renew surveillance of Carter Page, a former Trump campaign adviser suspected of acting as a Russian agent.

Boasberg, who previously served a seven-year term on the FISA Court, said Clinesmith’s alteration of the email undermined the court’s integrity but was a misguided mistake that provided Clinesmith no personal benefit. He sentenced Clinesmith to 12 months of probation and 400 hours of community service.

Boasberg said in his sentencing decision that he believed Clinesmith's role at the center of a years-long media "hurricane" had provided sufficient punishment.

item.title: Florida Senate nominee Angie Nixon says 'I don't know' when asked if she's capitalist or socialist
item.description: Angie Nixon repeatedly said "I don't know" when asked if she's a capitalist or socialist during a Politico "Conversation" interview Friday.
item.content:encoded:
Florida Democratic Senate nominee Angie Nixon struggled to identify whether she was a capitalist or socialist during an interview Friday, drawing sharp criticism from Republican Sen. Ashley Moody's campaign as the candidates entered the final week of Florida's Senate race.

Politico's Dasha Burns confronted the nominee over her membership in the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), noting that she had previously identified herself as a capitalist despite joining the socialist organization. When Burns pressed Nixon to explain how she personally identified, the Jacksonville Democrat repeatedly expressed uncertainty.

"I don't know. I don't know. Like, I don't know," Nixon said on "The Conversation."

"I identify as Angie Nixon, as a Black woman who was a former single mom, who wants to make sure that no one has to struggle the way I struggled when I was a single mom." 

LA MAYORAL HOPEFUL NITHYA RAMAN CALLS HERSELF BOTH A 'CAPITALIST' AND 'DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST'

Cameron Gambini, a spokesperson for Moody, criticized Nixon's response in a statement to Fox News Digital, questioning her ideological commitments and referencing a separate controversy surrounding her recent comments about Cuba.

"Angie Nixon voluntarily signed up to be a member of the Democrat Socialists," he said. "Now, she's clearly regretting letting her true colors shine. And just yesterday, she refused to say Cuba was a dictatorship. Socialist Angie is a radical lunatic who will never step foot on the Senate floor. Case closed."

When asked directly during an interview Monday with CBS News whether Nixon considered Cuba a dictatorship, she said, "You know, that is what people have told me. I have never been to Cuba, and so I will have to take their word for it."

Nixon subsequently challenged CBS News' characterization of her answer, maintaining that she believed Cubans who described their government as a dictatorship. CBS deleted its initial social media post and acknowledged that its description had inaccurately represented her response.

"It’s disappointing to have to say this, but [CBS News], this is a serious failure of editorial reporting," Nixon said in a post on X. "I clearly state in this clip that while I have not personally been to Cuba, I have spoken with Cubans who have described it as a dictatorship, and I believe them. To claim I declined to answer the question is categorically false.

"That is not journalism. It is misinformation."

Turning Point USA spokesman Andrew Kolvet criticized the Democratic nominee's response to Politico about whether she was a socialist in a statement to Fox News Digital, suggesting she was attempting to distance herself from socialism because of its political implications in Florida.

"Some pollster or political consultant probably told her socialism doesn’t sell in Florida," he said. "So, she’s offering the flimsiest and most insincere of explanations for how radical and economically illiterate she really and truly is. She seems to contend that existing within the land border of America makes you a capitalist.

"But just like existing in America doesn’t make someone an American, running for Senate doesn’t suddenly make Angie Nixon a good liar."

WHO IS ANGIE NIXON? BULLHORN-WIELDING SOCIALIST UPSETS ESTABLISHMENT FAVORITE IN SUNSHINE STATE STUNNER

Initially, in the same exchange on "The Conversation," Burns asked Nixon whether she considered herself a capitalist or socialist, prompting the Democratic nominee to first emphasize her support for government assistance programs.

"So, what I would say is, I live in a capitalistic society, and I just want to make sure that people have strong social programs and safety net programs because I've had to use them before," Nixon said. "So, you can call me whatever you want, but just know that I'm going to be out here working and fighting for hardworking and retired people and folks living with disabilities."

Throughout the interview, Nixon pushed back against political ideological branding, saying that she didn’t "care about labels" and considered herself a "humanist." She also said she remains a "lifelong Democrat" and noted that both she and her husband are small business owners who wouldn’t "want to take over anyone’s business." 

Nixon also explained that she joined the DSA due to local community work, noting how members helped her nonprofit when "the government shutdown happened" and people lost SNAP benefits. 

DSA CO-CHAIR MOCKED FOR PROUDLY CONFIRMING SOCIALISTS WANT TO ABOLISH THE SENATE, NATIONAL BORDERS, PRISONS

Nixon's uncertainty contrasted with her August appearance on NBC News' "Meet the Press" when host Kristen Welker pressed her about her DSA membership. During the interview, Nixon rejected the socialist label and explicitly embraced capitalism.

"I'm a capitalist who believes that we need some strong regulation," Nixon said.

Nixon joined the DSA in June but previously rejected several proposals in its national political program, including abolishing the U.S. Senate, drafting a new Constitution and defunding the military. 

The organization has also advocated public ownership of major corporations and essential industries, although it did not nationally endorse Nixon's campaign.

Nixon is challenging Moody, whom Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed to the U.S. Senate after Marco Rubio became secretary of state. 

Fox News Digital reached out to Nixon, CBS and the DSA for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: DAVID MARCUS: In Dallas, Talarico’s firewall is starting to show some real cracks
item.description: James Talarico faces lagging Black voter enthusiasm and suburban skepticism in Dallas, where he needs massive numbers to offset Ken Paxton's rural edge.
item.content:encoded:
I met Mark, in his late 50s, at an upscale restaurant in downtown Dallas. He is a lifelong Democrat and an immigration attorney, and, in general, is the kind of voter Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico needs not only to vote for him but to be excited to do so.

"My dad worked the railroad, made me go to college, we were LBJ [Lyndon B. Johnson] Democrats, and well, let’s just say, Talarico is obviously very different from Johnson, or even Ann Richards [Texas’ last Democratic governor, who served in the 1990s]."

Mark declined to tell me who he was voting for, or even whether he would vote, but I suspect Talarico can count on him, especially given Mark’s less-than-favorable view of Republican Ken Paxton. But there was no excitement when he talked about the race. Like so many others I spoke with, he said, "This isn’t like when Beto [O’Rourke] ran."

FOX NEWS POLL: IT’S A LONE STAR SENATE SHOWDOWN BETWEEN TALARICO AND PAXTON

If enthusiasm is a potential weak point for the Talarico campaign, then an even more worrisome one is his lagging support in the Black community, long the bedrock of Texas Democratic politics.

Jay and Darryl are two Black men in their 50s whom I met while they were having breakfast near the AT&T Discovery District. They each have very different ideas about what is going to happen Tuesday, when voters have their final say.

Jay told Fox News Digital of the Senate race, "Actually, I don’t think it's going to be close, he’s going to kill it, because he can get people to flip over," adding, "He would have had a harder time with [Sen. John] Cornyn."

Darryl, however, seemed less convinced, arguing that in Texas, "Conservatives aren’t loud, they don’t march, they don’t act up, they paint their hair, but I think they are the silent majority."

TALARICO SKIPS BERNIE SANDERS RALLY IN TEXAS, CAMPAIGNS SEPARATELY AS SENATE RACE HEATS UP

Both men agreed that Talarico’s failure to mend fences with his primary opponent, Rep. Jasmine Crockett, D-Texas, is a problem for Talarico, but they differed on how significant a problem it was, with Jay arguing, "She’s still helping, just down-ballot."

Carlos, who lives in Dallas and works in a hotel, told me over a cigar that looking "at the trajectory of America… I just don’t feel represented in any way." He went on to say, "I really wanted to believe it, the whole thing about no wars… my gas is super expensive from the people who said there was not going to be a war."

VOTERS PREPARE TO WEIGH IN ON TRUMP'S ECONOMY AS COSTS CONTINUE TO SURGE

This is good news for Talarico, in part because Carlos is a Joe Rogan fan who, though not a President Donald Trump voter, was open to the possibility that Trump could sway him, something that has not happened.

On the other side of the ledger for Talarico, or perhaps I should say for Paxton, is Debbie, a suburban mother who told Fox News Digital, "I’m a moderate, I have voted for Democrats, I voted for Beto, but Talarico just says so much crazy stuff, it's too much for Texas."

Had these conversations taken place across the Lone Star State, it might be good news for Talarico, but all of these people are in the Dallas area, where he needs to rack up major numbers to offset GOP dominance in rural areas.

On Tuesday, I spoke with GOP consultant Vinny Minchillo before we appeared on "The Will Cain Show." He said, "I do not like what I see in the early voting for Paxton." He estimated that the GOP was about 100,000 votes behind but acknowledged that, as a consultant, he never tries to paint a rosy picture.

TRUMP WON THIS RELIABLY RED STATE BY DOUBLE DIGITS. NOW A DEADLOCKED RACE IS BRINGING HIM BACK

When asked specifically about the early vote in the Black community, he told Fox News Digital, "It looks like it is down." So again, a mixed bag.

One wild-card issue that continues to come up in my conversations on the ground is the riots in France, with one voter telling me, "What if that was New York City, or D.C.? That doesn’t really seem impossible."

The GOP, especially at Vice President JD Vance’s rallies, has been hitting the France issue and what it says about unchecked immigration, hard in recent days, and I would expect that to continue.

Make no mistake, the Texas Senate race is tight, but if James Talarico cannot shore up the many votes he needs in Big D, it very well could leave Ken Paxton with enough votes in red counties to close the deal with Texas voters and help keep the Senate in Republican hands.

item.title: Mary Peltola's campaign, Dems backed covert scheme to field spoiler candidates in Alaska Senate race: report
item.description: Mary Peltola's campaign allegedly ran a covert "ballot composition project" to recruit namesake candidates and split the vote against Dan Sullivan.
item.content:encoded:
The campaign for Alaska Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola actively participated in an effort to peel votes away from incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan by recruiting namesake and spoiler candidates, according to an investigation The New York Times published Wednesday.

The covert operation, internally dubbed the "ballot composition project," allegedly involved aides from the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC), top campaign advisors, party lawyers and an operative who traveled across the state under assumed names.

In a series of posts on Truth Social, President Donald Trump said Peltola shouldn't be allowed to keep her name on the ballot, citing the instance as "ELECTION FRAUD."

The effort began in the summer of 2025, when a Peltola staffer was directed to comb through state voter rolls to compile a list of Alaskans named Dan Sullivan, according to the report. 

The plan worked earlier this year when Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher and left-leaning voter from Petersburg, switched his voter registration to Republican shortly before filing his candidacy in the Senate race.

TRUMP SAYS 'WE ARE LOOKING INTO' OTHER DAN SULLIVAN ON ALASKA BALLOT, WARNS ABOUT GOVERNOR'S RACE

PERSONAL ATTACKS FLY AS SULLIVAN, PELTOLA SPAR OVER CORRUPTION, CHARACTER AND CONTROVERSY

Elisa Rios, Peltola’s former campaign manager who was fired in August, told the Times that while Peltola was not directly involved in orchestrating the project, she was "definitely aware."

"Alaskan voters need to know," Rios said. "There was a lot of speculation, and voters should get the full picture when making their decisions."

Rios later attempted to retract her comments prior to publication, but the newspaper noted that her initial interviews were corroborated by text messages, internal documents and 11 other sources.

Central to the plan was Democratic operative Jerid Kurtz, who allegedly traveled through Alaska using aliases such as "Zane," the report states.

TOP ELECTION SCHEMES ROILING KEY MIDTERM RACES AS BOTH PARTIES ACCUSE RIVALS OF TRICKERY

Kurtz allegedly met potential recruits at local pubs and diners, offering outside financial backing to persuade conservative and independent candidates to run and split the right-leaning vote.

"The Democrats cheated!" Trump wrote. "They found a man named Dan Sullivan, put him on the Ballot, then lied to the Court, and said they didn’t know anything about it. That’s perjury. She shouldn’t be allowed to run, and neither should the FAKE Dan Sullivan!" 

"Peltola should suffer the Legal and Political consequences for what she has done, A FRAUD ON THE AMERICAN PUBLIC, and Dan Sullivan should be allowed to run without either Mary Peltola or FAKE Dan Sullivan on the Ballot," he added.

Beyond the second Sullivan, operatives recruited other potential candidates, including drywall contractor Gerald Heikes, according to the report.

GOP SENATOR, EX-HOUSE DEM EMERGE FROM ALASKA’S ‘JUNGLE PRIMARY’ DESPITE FAR-LEFT MEDDLING

They also allegedly successfully pressured progressive candidate David Leslie to drop out of the race to avoid siphoning votes from Peltola, paving the way for Heikes to claim the fourth spot on Alaska’s ranked-choice ballot.

Campaign advisors and the DSCC also weighed creating a third-party "MAGA party" to siphon votes from the incumbent senator before abandoning the idea in May, according to the report.

Jacquelyn Lopez, an attorney with the prominent Democratic firm Elias Law Group, which represents both the DSCC and Peltola’s campaign, was looped into discussions regarding the third-party strategy and field operations, the Times wrote.

Internal messages allegedly showed staff asking whether they needed to "follow up with Jackie about maga party stuff," while another noted that Lopez was in touch with Kurtz.

"The Alaskans for Mary campaign has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign and did not recruit any candidates into the race," Peltola’s campaign said in a statement to the Times. The DSCC echoed that stance, stating it had no role in recruiting either Sullivan or any other Republican candidate.

In a statement to Fox News, the DSCC said it was not involved with Dan J. Sullivan, while pointing to Republicans' allegations of political shenanigans.

"Republicans have a long history of recruiting and propping up candidates in an attempt to boost their own campaigns, including recruiting a prisoner with a New York address to run against Mary Peltola and spending nearly half a million dollars to secure a spot on the ballot in Alaska for an Arizona resident in the Senate race this cycle," a DSCC spokesperson said.

The White House pointed to a social media post by Communications Director Steven Cheung on X: "BREAKING: Democrats' secret, CORRUPT plan to stack Alaska's ballot EXPOSED!"

The report came just days before Election Day and amid a Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of the election if the incumbent Sullivan loses due to voter confusion over the two identical candidate names.

Under Alaska's four-person general election system, Peltola enters Tuesday as the sole Democrat on the ballot, facing off against Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, Dan J. Sullivan and Gerald Heikes.

item.title: UCF gets another big win by dodging a field-storming fine after stunning upset over BYU
item.description: UCF Knights avoided a Big 12 field-storming fine after their overtime upset of the No. 2 BYU Cougars thanks to thorough safety preparations.
item.content:encoded:
The UCF Knights pulled off one of the biggest wins in program history when they beat the BYU Cougars in an overtime thriller on Saturday.

Now, the school has earned a victory that the athletic department might be even more excited about: not getting fined for the post-game field-storming.

Field-storming sometimes gets a bad rap, but if ever there was a time for it, beating the No. 2 team in the country when you're unranked is probably it.

TEXAS BANS FAN WHO WAS CAUGHT FLIPPING OFF FLORIDA PLAYERS IN POSTGAME VIDEO FOLLOWING GATORS' UPSET

So, that's what Knights fans did ... even if it was a little tricky getting down the field at Acrisure Bounce House.

Alright, so they might need to pony up a few bucks for more canopies, but they won't need to pay the Big 12 as a mea culpa for the field storming.

Why not?

Because it turns out that the school did such a good job preparing and implementing a plan in the event of a good ol' fashioned field stormin' that there's no need for a fine.

MARYLAND IS GOING TO SOME EMBARRASSING LENGTHS TO MAKE SURE STUDENTS STAY UNTIL THE END OF GAMES

"We provided the Big 12 Conference w/thorough documentation of our safety preparations, including coordinated escorts for visiting players, coaches & officials," said UCF athletic director Terry Mohajir, per On3's Brett McMurphy. "We’re proud of our athletics staff for their planning, preparation & execution in helping protect everyone involved."

So the trick to not having to cut a check after a field storm is to prepare for a field storm.

Paradoxically, if you're expecting a field storming ... then maybe that win is not worth storming the field.

But while there's no way UCF came into that game thinking they'd be beating a really solid BYU team, it happened, and they were ready.

Which, in the end, saved them a heck of a lot of money.
